\section{Per-system sensitivity}
\label{app:persys}

The limit Table~\ref{tab:persys} quotes for a system is that of its best
window, a bound pair appearing under its primary's name. A window inside the
attribution mask constrains nothing (\S\ref{sec:summary}) and cannot be a best
window. Beside each limit are that window's centre frequency $\nu$ and channel
width $\Delta\nu$, the system's merged coverage $\Delta\nu_{\rm cov}$, the
percentage \emph{dec.} by which atmospheric decorrelation leaves the limit
optimistic, and whether blocks of different sessions cover a common frequency
more than a day (d) or a year (yr) apart, over the census and the \ZcNRecEB{}
blocks the recurrence test reads. A dagger marks the \SmcNMeasSys{} of the
\NSysALim{} systems whose own best window was one of the \SensNInj{} injected
into; the other \SmcNEstSys{} limits are transferred from the class average
and carry the dispersion observed between injected windows,
$\times\SmcDispLo$ to $\times\SmcDispHi$, itself transferred for the
\NgNExtrapSys{} \NgExtrapSysNoun{} whose best window lies outside the injected
range in band, channel width, array configuration or integration time. A
section mark flags the \FcNSys{} limits set in a block whose fields were
recombined after the limits were computed, which are conservative
(\S\ref{sec:pninetysel}). Each
system's limit at both ends of the calibration interval, with decorrelation
and with the exact channel response divided out, and its probability of
reaching $10^{15}$\,W when its transferred windows draw their factors from the
injected ones, are in \texttt{sensitivity/\allowbreak system\_limits.csv} of
the data archive; the full treatment is in
\texttt{documentation/\allowbreak appendix\_F\_per\_system.md}
\citep{SIdeposit}.

therefore a mixture, \NgDecMeasMedPct{} per cent over the measured systems
and \NgDecImpMedPct{} over the imputed. The imputed blocks are not a random
subset: \NbDecPctTwelveUn{} per cent are 12\,m against
\NbDecPctTwelveMeas{} per cent of those with a record, that array's long
baselines being what loses coherence. Their windows lose
\RpDecMatchMed{} per cent in the median, and \RpDecMatchHi{} per cent had each
performed like the ninetieth-percentile block matched to it, a condition on a
calibration performance the archive does not report. Every value in the
column is a floor: the phase rms is recorded on the calibrator, not on the
target.\par}
